title: Measurement of the maximum oxygen uptake VO2max: VO2peak is no longer acceptable
claims: A VO2 plateau during incremental exercise is not an obligatory outcome and is absent in at least 40% of healthy subjects even when VO2max is actually achieved.
The absence of a plateau is more common in children, older adults, very unfit people and patients with cardiovascular or pulmonary disease.
Secondary criteria such as respiratory exchange ratio, age-predicted maximal heart rate and blood lactate are unreliable substitutes for confirming VO2max.
VO2peak, defined simply as the highest VO2 reached in a test, cannot distinguish a true upper limit from test termination for other reasons.
A verification phase can be used when no plateau is observed.
